subject: Phased ramp & commit adjustment for 8→16 GPU reserved pool
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@pixisai.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Capacity increase request: reserved GPUs

Monica —

Quick note from our infra team: we’re expecting a sustained jump in inference volume after next month’s model rollout and want to move our Dedicated pool from 8 → 16 GPUs at renewal. Can you share a realistic timeline, pricing impact (monthly commit change), and any options to phase the activation to limit cold-start risk? Procurement will need an outline we can attach to the internal ask.

Key asks:
- Can we stage the capacity (e.g., +4 / +4 / +? over a quarter)?
- What happens to billing in a partial-month cutover?
- Any throughput guarantees or SLAs for the expanded pool?

Appreciate speedy guidance — they’re hoping to finalize budget by 11/30.

—Samir
Director of Infrastructure
PixisAI
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@pixisai.com>
Cc: PixisAI Procurement <procurement@pixisai.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity increase request: reserved GPUs

Samir —

Thanks for the heads up. We can absolutely support a lift from 8 → 16 reserved GPUs at renewal and, given your timeline, I recommend a phased activation that balances availability risk and cashflow. High-level proposal below (attaching a capacity workbook with cost math).

Phased ramp proposal (recommended):
- Month 0 (renewal effective date): commit increases to 12 GPUs (+4)
- Month 2: scale to 16 GPUs (+4)
- Billing: pro-rata charges for partial months; we smooth incremental charges across the first billing quarter to limit one-time billing shock
- Throughput & SLA: we’ll attach a 95th-percentile per-request latency target for the 16-GPU pool and a throughput guardrail (x tokens/sec per GPU). If we miss the latency SLO for more than two full days in a 30-day window, we provide a service credit (detailed in the amendment)

Commercial note: the monthly committed spend will be updated to reflect 16 GPUs (pro-rated based on your current instance profile). Because this is a mid-size expansion we can offer a limited volume discount on the incremental commit — details in the workbook.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick 30-min call this week to walk the workbook and confirm the activation windows
2) If agreed, we’ll prepare a one-page amendment and a DocuSign envelope for signature
3) Ops will schedule the staged activations and can run a short canary for the first +4 GPUs

Attaching: capacity_workbook.xlsx (cost math, activation calendar).

Are you free Thursday 11/13 or Friday 11/14 for a quick sync?

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Capacity increase request — pricing + SLA ask

Marissa / Sean —

Looping you both to confirm commercial levers and the SLA language for PixisAI. Client wants to move 8→16 at renewal with a phased ramp. Key points:
- We want to offer billing smoothing across Q1 to avoid a large one-time invoice for them
- Ops requests a canary window for first +4 GPUs; they’ll want a 48–72 hour warmup and KV-cache priming run
- Procurement will expect DocuSign-ready amendment and clear service credit language for missed latency SLOs

Draft terms attached in the workbook; I also sketched a one-page amendment (not legally final). Two asks:
1) Can we provide up to 12% discount on the *incremental* commit for the first 12 months? (they’re mid-market but high-growth)
2) Are we comfortable with the proposed SLO/service credit formula or should legal tighten it before I send to the buyer?

Quick replies preferred — procurement wants numbers by 11/19.

Monica —

Thanks for the clear summary. High level: approve the commercial posture with the following constraints.

Discount & commercial:
- Approve up to 12% discount on the incremental commit for months 1–12 (applies only to the delta from 8 → 16)
- Require minimum 12-month renewed term on the *new* commit to protect margin

SLO & ops:
- Ops should run a canary for the first +4 GPUs with a 72-hour observation period; we’ll include an explicit fallback to revert to 12 GPUs if a repeatable regression appears
- For the SLO/service credit, change language to cap aggregate credit at one month of incremental spend; legal to review before sending externally

Docs & activation:
- Prepare a one-page amendment and attach a draft_amendment_v1.pdf; send via DocuSign with a 10-business-day signature window

I’m good for the DocuSign flow — please copy me on the envelope. Also flag finance so we can model the prorated charges.

Marissa

Cc: PixisAI Procurement <procurement@pixisai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Nov 2027 17:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity increase request: phased activation & amendment (DocuSign)

Samir —

Thanks again for the call last week. Per our discussion here’s the agreed path and next steps so procurement has everything it needs to approve the budget: 

Agreed commercial summary:
- Commit: move from 8 → 16 GPUs, effective at renewal date. Pricing in attached draft amendment reflects a pro-rated smoothing of the first quarter charges.
- Incremental discount: 12% applied only to the incremental monthly commit for months 1–12.
- Minimum term: new commit locked for 12 months.

Operational plan:
- Phase 1 (day 0): activate +4 GPUs (12 total). Run a 72-hour canary and latency baseline collection.
- Phase 2 (month 2): activate remaining +4 GPUs (16 total). Ops will notify 72 hours before activation and provide a short regression report after each step.
- Fallback: if we observe a repeatable latency regression, Ops will revert to previous capacity and we’ll remediate before retrying activation.

SLO & credits (summary):
- 95th-percentile latency target for the 16-GPU pool. Credits capped at one month of incremental spend for any 30-day window with repeated misses. Full language in amendment.

Attached: draft_amendment_v1.pdf (one-page amendment), capacity_workbook.xlsx (cost math). DocuSign envelope: https://www.docusign.com/tx/7f3b9e4a — I’ve initiated it and copied Marissa on the envelope. Please review and sign within 10 business days so we can meet your 11/30 internal deadline.

If procurement wants a slightly different billing smoothing profile we can adjust the workbook — happy to update if you send a target invoice profile.

Best regards,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
